quiz.explain: A validity date protects you from price rises after the quote is accepted much later.

quiz.q: A quote is ₦60,000 above the client's budget. What is the best response?
options: Tell the client to save up and come back
Remove the contingency without telling them
Offer options such as cheaper fabric, a feature wall or doing the work in phases
quiz.explain: Options keep the design quality and respect the budget without undervaluing your work.

quiz.q: Which is an honest way to build your first portfolio?
options: Post photos of rooms from Pinterest
Ask a friend to write reviews of work you have not done
Decorate a relative's parlour and document it with permission
Use a famous designer's project with your logo
quiz.explain: Your portfolio must show only your own real work; a documented family or community project counts.

quiz.q: Before posting a client's room online, what should you remove or blur?
options: Family photos, documents, house numbers and children's faces
quiz.explain: Protect the client's privacy and security by removing personal and location details, and post only with permission.

finalQuiz.q: What is the main difference between interior decoration and interior design?
options: Decoration works with the existing structure; design may change walls, layout and services
finalQuiz.explain: Decorators style the room as built; structural, electrical and plumbing changes belong to designers and qualified trades.

finalQuiz.q: A room has all its dark, heavy furniture against one wall. Which fix best improves balance?
options: Add more items to the same wall
Move a heavy item, such as a tall cabinet, to the opposite wall
finalQuiz.explain: Spreading visual weight across both sides balances the room.

finalQuiz.q: A client loves indigo with small rust-orange details. Which scheme is this closest to?
finalQuiz.explain: Blue and orange tones sit roughly opposite on the colour wheel, making a complementary scheme.

finalQuiz.q: Using 60-30-10, which plan fits a bedroom best?
options: Walls, curtains and cushions all in equal bright red
Accent colour on 60% of the room
Walls 60% soft neutral, curtains and bedspread 30% blue, cushions and art 10% rust
finalQuiz.explain: Dominant neutral walls, a secondary colour in large fabrics and a small repeated accent follow the guide.

finalQuiz.q: A wardrobe is 120 cm wide. At a scale of 1:50, how wide is its cut-out?
Which pair is ambient and task lighting, in that order?
finalQuiz.explain: Ambient light fills the room; task light is focused light for an activity such as homework.

finalQuiz.q: An LED box says 800 lm, 3000 K. What does this tell you?
options: It gives roughly the light of an old 60 W bulb in a warm white colour
It is a dim cool daylight bulb
It only works on solar power
finalQuiz.explain: About 800 lumens is roughly an old 60 W bulb, and around 3000 K is warm white.

finalQuiz.q: Track 2.4 m, fullness 2, fabric 1.4 m wide, cut drop 2.6 m, plain fabric. How many metres?
Walls total 42 m² with 4 m² of openings. Two coats, coverage 10 m² per litre. How much paint?
finalQuiz.explain: Net area 38 m² × 2 coats = 76 m²; 76 ÷ 10 = 7.6 litres.

finalQuiz.q: You bought materials for ₦95,000 from a ₦110,000 client float (illustrative). What should you give the client?
options: Nothing; the balance is your tip
Receipts, a purchase table and the ₦15,000 balance returned or credited as agreed
Only the receipts for the most expensive items
finalQuiz.explain: Transparent accounts, all receipts and returning or crediting the balance keep trust.

finalQuiz.q: Which item must be in the client brief before you quote?
options: Budget, timeline, must-keep items and the room's purpose
finalQuiz.explain: These define what you can do, for how much and by when.

options: One total on a WhatsApp message
A verbal price at the market
A price that changes after each purchase
Itemised materials, labour, transport, fee and contingency, with scope, validity and payment terms
finalQuiz.explain: An itemised quote with clear terms protects both sides and builds trust.

capstone.title: Interior Decoration Transformation Project
capstone.brief: Decorate one real room for a client, relative or your own household, and produce a documented project file showing the brief, plan, budget, quotation, before and after photos, the reasons for your key decisions and an honest reflection on budget and feedback.
steps: Run a client brief and site visit, take before photos from fixed spots and get the brief confirmed in writing.
Measure the room and draw a 1:50 floor plan with your proposed layout.
Choose a colour scheme using the colour wheel and 60-30-10, and make a mood board.
Plan lighting layers and calculate fabric and paint quantities.
Write an itemised budget and quotation with a 10% contingency and agree it.
Carry out the makeover safely, then inspect it with the finishing checklist.
Take after photos from the same spots, track budget versus actual and collect feedback after two weeks.
evidence: Confirmed brief and before photos from every corner
1:50 floor plan with layout and lighting marked
Mood board with colour scheme and samples
Itemised quotation and budget versus actual table with receipts
Matching before and after photo pairs
Explanation of key decisions linked to the room's function and household needs
Client or household feedback and an honest reflection on budget adherence
